I don't think so that their is state law like that. but it is possible that mattress store have policy like that.

You can always sue. Whether you can win is another story. You did not indicate why you believe the mattress is defective, which would help answer your question. If it is a manufacturer's defect, the manufacturer will likely stand behind their product and replace it. This is certainly dependent on the brand, but all the majors have Mfg warranties that would cover most defects.

That said, the store can have whatever return policy they like. They are not required to have one, and can refuse any return. As far as a law forbidding the return, I can't find any, and because most mattress stores I looked at have a return policy, I can't imagine this to be true. The store does, however, have to post their return policy.

According to the Ohio Attorney General

Sellers are not required to have any specific type of return policy under Ohio law. However, if a store has a refund policy, it must be clearly and conspicuously posted (R.C. 1345.03(B)(7)).

A refund policy may not be printed only on the receipt, because the consumer sees the receipt after the purchase has been made. If a seller does not have a refund policy posted, the consumer is entitled to a refund, if the consumer requests it.

Ohio law does not prohibit restocking fees, or fees for returning an item to the shelves. Nevertheless, sellers should clearly and conspicuously disclose any restocking fees before the consumer makes a purchase.
